title: 3. Unit Economics, Margin Architecture & FY26 Waterfall
book_title: Chapter 3: Follow Every ₹100 — Margin Compression, Cost Structure & Cash Conversion

epigraph.quote: Revenue growth without margin discipline is just busywork; true compounding shows up in how many rupees of free cash flow survive out of every hundred rupees billed.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

summary: In FY26 (ended March 2026), Cyient generated ₹7,268 Cr in consolidated revenue (-1% YoY) and ₹899 Cr in operating profit (12.4% OPM, down from 18.2% in FY24), converting ₹463 Cr into net profit and ₹693 Cr into free cash flow. While DET EBIT margins compressed to 12.2% in FY26 amid wage hikes and weak utilization before recovering to 14.2% in Q2 FY27, the group's consolidated margin ceiling is structurally capped by the lower-margin DLM manufacturing mix.

web_blocks.html: Cyient's audited FY26 (March 2026) income statement shows the margin compression that drove its strategic reset [1]. Consolidated sales edged down 1.2% YoY from ₹7,360 Cr in FY25 to ₹7,268 Cr in FY26 [1]. Operating expenses rose from ₹6,222 Cr to ₹6,369 Cr over the same period [1]. As a result, operating profit (EBITDA) fell from ₹1,138 Cr (15.5% OPM) in FY25 and ₹1,303 Cr (18.2% OPM) in FY24 to ₹899 Cr (12.4% OPM) in FY26 [1].

web_blocks.takeaway: Even as accounting PAT margin fell by 347 bps from FY24 to FY26, Cyient actually expanded its Free Cash Flow margin from 9.07% to 9.54% (₹693 Cr) by keeping capex disciplined at ₹94 Cr and collecting receivables.

web_blocks.caption: Quarterly Margin & Below-the-Line Inflection (Q1 FY26 – Q2 FY27)
web_blocks.takeaway: Quarterly OPM bottomed at 12% in FY26 and recovered to 14% in Q2 FY27, but rising interest (₹14 Cr to ₹37 Cr), higher depreciation (₹68 Cr to ₹84 Cr), and an elevated 33–36% effective tax rate kept Q2 FY27 PAT (₹132 Cr) below Q2 FY26 (₹143 Cr).

web_blocks.html: Three forces explain why Cyient's unit economics shifted between FY24 and Q2 FY27. First is mix dilution and upfront hardware spending. Cyient DLM grew 26.5% YoY in Q2 FY27 [2]. Yet build-to-print EMS runs at ~10–11% EBITDA margins. Upfront sales hires and memory tightness also narrowed DLM's net margin [3][7]. Second is FY26 operating deleverage and M&A friction. DET sales flattened in FY25–FY26 while wage hikes and bench costs persisted [4]. Beyond the ₹42.3 Cr Labour Code charge, audited FY26 MD&A discloses two major drags on profit. Cyient booked ₹71.2 Cr (₹712 Mn) in fees for an aborted acquisition and ₹27.8 Cr (₹278 Mn) of tooling goodwill impairment [4][5][8].

Third, Q2 FY27 margin gains now meet higher financing, R&D, and FX costs. Under Sukamal Banerjee, DET EBIT margin rebounded 206 bps YoY to a 10-quarter high of 14.2% (₹237 Cr) [6]. However, the consolidated P&L absorbs new drags absent in FY26. Cyient Semi posted a -₹30 Cr Q2 EBIT loss on product R&D, pulling group EBIT margin to 10.2% [9]. Management targets FY28 Semi breakeven amid foundry and memory limits [9]. Below EBIT, quarterly interest jumped from ₹14 Cr in Q4 FY26 to ₹37 Cr in Q2 FY27. Depreciation rose from ₹68 Cr to ₹84 Cr as Kinetic and TAO joined the books, while tax rates hit 33–36% [1][10]. Standalone Q2 also booked a ₹46.0 Cr net FX loss (vs ₹9.3 Cr gain YoY), collapsing Other Income [1][10]. Full-period interest on ₹2,759 Cr of debt will test whether DET and Semi margins can outpace these costs.

web_blocks.title: Capex Discipline vs. M&A Capital Intensity
paragraphs: On a purely organic basis, Cyient looks asset-light: FY26 capex was only ₹94 Cr (1.3% of sales), allowing ₹787 Cr of CFO to translate into ₹693 Cr of Free Cash Flow.

Yet including M&A (₹1,006 Cr investing outflow in FY23, ₹71.2 Cr of aborted-deal expenses in FY26, plus the $85M Kinetic and $218M TAO Digital deals in 2026), Cyient's true reinvestment rate is far higher—meaning organic FCF overstates steady-state owner earnings if serial acquisitions are required to sustain growth.

book_paragraphs: Let us walk through every ₹100 that came through Cyient's door in FY26, because the consolidated income statement tells two very different stories depending on whether you look at accounting profit or cash flow. In FY26, Cyient billed ₹7,268 Cr of revenue, roughly flat against ₹7,360 Cr the year before. Out of every ₹100 of sales, ₹87.63 went straight out to operating expenses—engineer salaries, component purchases for DLM, subcontractors, a one-time ₹42.3 Cr employee benefit provision for India's new Labour Codes, and ₹71.2 Cr of due-diligence and legal costs from an aborted acquisition that never closed (alongside ₹27.8 Cr of goodwill impairment in the tooling business). That left just ₹12.37 of operating profit, down sharply from ₹18.23 just two years earlier in FY24.

Follow the rest of that ₹100 down the waterfall. Depreciation and amortization took ₹3.82, interest cost took ₹0.84, and other income added back ₹1.16, leaving ₹8.86 of pre-tax profit. After paying ₹2.49 in taxes—an effective tax rate that crept up from 23% in FY24 to 28% in FY26—Cyient kept just ₹6.37 as net profit, or ₹463 Cr for the full year. On an accounting basis, margins had been squeezed by nearly 350 basis points in two years.

Yet here is the twist that separates a real business from a fragile one: out of that same ₹100 of revenue, Cyient converted ₹10.83 into operating cash flow (₹787 Cr) and, after spending only ₹1.29 (₹94 Cr) on capital expenditure, generated ₹9.54 of Free Cash Flow (₹693 Cr). In other words, even in its worst margin year of the decade, Cyient's free cash flow margin actually ticked higher than in FY24 because management tightened receivables and kept organic capex lean.

Why did operating margins compress so hard from 18% to 12% in the first place? Two reasons. First, Cyient DLM—the manufacturing subsidiary—grows faster than services, and electronics manufacturing structurally runs at 10–11% EBITDA margins because raw-material components pass through the P&L, while upfront sales-leadership investments and memory-component tightness have weighed on DLM's near-term margins. Second, when DET's organic growth stalled in FY25, Cyient could not cut senior engineering bench costs fast enough, resulting in classic negative operating leverage.

Now look at the quarterly inflection from Q1 FY26 through Q2 FY27, because it shows both the operational healing and the new financial friction. Operating margins bottomed at 12% in Q2 and Q4 FY26 and climbed back to 14% in Q2 FY27, powered by DET's 14.2% EBIT margin—a ten-quarter high. Yet Q2 FY27 consolidated net profit of ₹132 Cr was still lower than Q2 FY26's ₹143 Cr! Why? Look across the segments and below the operating line: Cyient Semiconductors posted a -₹30 Cr EBIT loss from product R&D (pulling group EBIT margin down to 10.2%), the standalone company absorbed a ₹46.0 Cr net foreign exchange loss (collapsing other income from ₹71 Cr to ₹9 Cr), interest more than doubled from ₹16 Cr to ₹37 Cr, depreciation jumped from ₹72 Cr to ₹84 Cr, and the effective tax rate spiked to 33%. Going forward, every rupee of DET margin recovery will have to clear a much higher R&D, FX, interest, amortization, and tax bar.

book_callouts.title: The Acquirer's Cash Flow Illusion
book_callouts.text: When a company spends just 1.3% of sales on organic capex but deploys ₹2,500+ Cr on acquisitions every few years, treating 'CFO minus organic Capex' as pure distributable Free Cash Flow is dangerous. You have to judge whether the acquired businesses generate enough incremental cash to pay back their purchase price.

book_subsections.title: DET Margin Recovery vs. Structural DLM Mix
paragraphs: Management previously targeted 16% DET EBIT margins, then recalibrated under Sukamal Banerjee toward a steady 15% medium-term goal. Reaching 14.2% in Q2 FY27 shows real progress on utilization, pyramid optimization, and offshoring.

Still, you should never expect Cyient's consolidated group OPM to return to the 18% levels of FY22–FY24 unless DLM's share shrinks or Semiconductors scales into high-margin catalog silicon. A 14–15% consolidated EBITDA margin is a more realistic structural steady state for a services-plus-manufacturing hybrid.

Notice also how volatile Other Income was in FY26—swinging from +₹70–71 Cr in H1 FY26 to -₹45 Cr in Q4 FY26 due to foreign exchange and treasury movements. Stripping out Other Income noise makes it clear that core operating profit recovery is real, but bottom-line EPS growth will lag until debt is paid down.
